To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Ojibwes’ food sovereignty is threatened and that this is a violation of the White Pine treaty.

1) the treaties established between the US and American Indian nations recognize the Ojibwes’ political sovereignty, 2) the treaties also recognize the Ojibs’ right to food sovereignty, 3) the treaties recognize the Ojibus’ right to maintain traditional relationships between their culture and the natural world, 4) appropriation of wild rice threatens the Ojibws’ political sovereignty, and 5) the US is violating the White Pine Treaty.

(a) the White Pine Treaty of the Ojibiwe and U.S. government in 1837 established the Ojibwes’ right to hunt, trap, and gather in their territory, and (b) the treaty’s recognition of this right implies the right to food sovereignty, which is threatened by the appropriation of wild rice.

understanding the implications of the White Pine treaty for Ojibwe sovereignty and the implications of Ojibwe political sovereignty for food sovereignty.
